chunks: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, repels through supplication the matter which He knew would be supplicated for, and so He responds. And if the servant had not been granted success in making that supplication, he would have been struck by it — by something that would bend his face to the earth.

key_terms.جَدِيدِ الْأَرْضِ: surface of the earth — the phrase emphasizes the severity of the fall
key_terms.لَيَدْفَعُ: repels/wards off — present tense, emphatic lam, indicating certainty
key_terms.يَجُثُّهُ: prostrates/bends him to the earth — image of humiliation under affliction

ai.seo_question: Does supplication (du'a) repel divine afflictions in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) teaches that supplication has a real and transformative effect in warding off afflictions, not merely as a pious act but as a divinely ordained mechanism. Allah, in His foreknowledge, has built du'a into the very fabric of fate: He already knows which afflictions will be averted because a servant will supplicate, and those servants He grants the tawfiq (divine enablement) to supplicate. Conversely, when supplication is withheld, the affliction falls with crushing force.
word_analysis: would bend him down / prostrate him
